assumptions: Recovery is attributed to the flag revert on the basis of timing — the service returned to baseline shortly after the flag was set off — rather than on an independent test that the flag was the only thing that changed.
The defect is assumed to predate the lookback window: no deploy or release was found in the change events searched, so the age and origin of the faulty code were not established.

input.executive_summary: Shortly before midnight UTC a new account-spending feature was switched on for all shoppers of the online shop. The newly enabled code failed whenever a shopper's account page was assembled without the data it expected, so a large share of account-page views returned errors instead of loading. Customers trying to view their account during this window would have seen failures; other parts of the shop were unaffected, and no data was lost or altered. The problem began at 23:56Z on 22 September and the service was back to normal by 00:01Z on 23 September. The automated on-call system detected the alert, traced the failures to the feature being switched on, and turned the feature back off, after which the account page recovered and was confirmed healthy. A draft code fix for the underlying defect has been opened for the owning team to review; the feature should stay off until that fix ships.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled from off to fully on between 23:55 and 23:56Z, exposing a code path in `src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:626` that calls `max()` on an empty iterable and raises `ValueError` while rendering the account page. No deploy occurred in the change window, so the defect was latent in already-running code and was only exercised once the flag enabled it; turning the flag back off returned the service to baseline.
